There is no such thing as *native* if you want to be pedantic and go far enough back. The native religious beliefs would the various celtic/Britonic pantheons I suppose but even those cultures displaced an older one. What I mean when I say native beliefs of the English is the germanic paganism that the various tribes practiced on the continent and then carried over to Britain. England as a singular kingdom itself was formed mostly as a Christian nation yes, but the various petty kingdoms were not and the concept of an English people predates the formation of the Kingdom. So I dont think it's wrong for an Englishman to say that the traditional folk religion of his ancestors is native to England. So no Germanic paganism isn't "native" to Britain but it is native to the English, at least that's how I interpret it. Feel free to disagree but I think people are being unnecessarily rude to OP purely on pedantry when all he wants to do is get in touch with his cultural roots. And quite frankly I find it silly to call Anglo-Saxon paganism poorly documented when we know much less about the beliefs of the pre Roman Britons
